Calculating Gholdengo's scarf-boosted speed against Rotom-Wash, weighing how resisted Make It Rain would be versus neutral Shadow Ball, and considering whether Tricking the scarf onto Rotom could cripple it while costing Gholdengo its speed edge.

Shadow Ball math works out to roughly a 55% hit on Rotom, a solid 2HKO, and stays useful against most of their team aside from Kingambit's Dark resistance and Mimikyu's Disguise. Given Kingambit's sucker punch threat, I'll go with Shadow Ball here.

decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Garchomp sits at 54% after the first Shadow Ball, and a second likely won't quite finish it off unless I get lucky with the roll or a SpD drop. I need to weigh the risk since Garchomp threatens back with Earthquake, which could seriously dent or even knock out Gholdengo despite its speed advantage from the Scarf.

My alternative is switching to my own Garchomp, though Mega Evolution isn't available right now, likely because the active Pokémon isn't the mega-capable one. Still, I'm leaning toward firing off Shadow Ball again since I move first and might just clinch the KO before their Earthquake becomes a problem — plus I want to preserve Gholdengo since it's valuable against their own nearly-dead Gholdengo and the lurking Rotom-Wash.

Running the math, Shadow Ball looks like it OHKOs their Gholdengo even without heavy investment, but the real question is the trade — if their Garchomp survives at around 8% after the exchange, Kingambit's Sucker Punch can finish it off, leaving their side down to just the 1% Gholdengo and Rotom against my remaining team.

Switching Garchomp in is risky since EQ still does heavy damage and a predicted Dragon Claw isn't guaranteed to OHKO given the speed tie uncertainty. Bringing in Kingambit instead eats a super-effective EQ but survives thanks to its bulk, which might be the safer play here.

Then Sucker Punch from Kingambit should finish off a weakened Garchomp, though I'm left with low HP. Shadow Ball could still work if my earlier roll wasn't max damage, and there's a chance the opponent switches out instead of pressing the attack, but I should plan around them clicking EQ since that's the most threatening line against me.

Switching Kingambit in predicting EQ would take too much damage, around 85%, so that's not a good option. I'll just go with Shadow Ball.
